description: I am looking for team members who are enthusiastic, collaborative, and eager to learn. Skills in AI/ML, software development, web development, data visualization, UI/UX design, and research would be valuable. Most importantly, I appreciate people who communicate well, contribute ideas, and are motivated to turn concepts into working prototypes
summary: Ghosts of Space is a browser-based 3D experience that reveals what humanity leaves behind in space. We developed an interactive universe, built with Python, JavaScript and Three.js, where visitors scroll through a live model of Earth, the Moon, Mars and a belt of orbiting debris, alongside pages on the equipment discarded on the Moon and Mars. The project addresses the challenge by turning open NASA and ESA knowledge into a visual story that anyone can explore on a phone or computer, with no installation or technical background. Each page presents short facts drawn from NASA and ESA sources, so learning feels like exploration. It is important because thousands of dead satellites and fragments now circle Earth, and abandoned hardware rests on other worlds, yet most people never see this legacy. Awareness is the first step toward cleaner orbits, responsible mission design and respect for the places we explore. Our demo video presents the idea in thirty seconds.
details: Our project, Ghosts of Space, is a live 3D web experience that lets visitors explore Earth, the Moon and Mars and discover the machines left behind in space. Every scene is rendered in real time in the browser, so no installation is needed, and the content is based on open NASA and ESA data. We hope it makes the problem of abandoned equipment and orbital debris easier to understand, and encourages support for responsible mission design. The site was coded in Python, HTML, CSS, JavaScript,React,Vite,Oxlint and Three.js. Animation for the demo video came from Google Flow (Veo), voice-over from ElevenLabs, and editing from InShot and Kapwing, while Gemini, ChatGPT and Claude helped with ideas, scripts and code. Our creativity lies in presenting forgotten spacecraft as living "ghosts" inside an immersive 3D world, turning facts into something visitors can see, explore and remember.
